meta.title: Significant flood risk areas in Finland (SYKE)

conventions.floodTypes: river = vesistötulva (every inland area on the list is on a river; the published type does not split river from lake), sea = meritulva, stormwater = hulevesitulva. floodTypesPublished keeps SYKE's own Finnish value, which also names ice jams (jääpato), frazil-ice jams (hyydepato) and floods caused by a structure (rakenteesta aiheutuva tulva, here the Kyrkösjärvi dam).
conventions.designated: year of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry decision of 19 December 2024 (3rd round). SYKE's attribute raportointivuosi is 2025, the year reported to the EU.
conventions.municipalities: worked out by overlaying SYKE's published area polygons on Statistics Finland's 2026 municipal boundaries (statfi-municipalities-2026); a municipality is listed when it holds the largest part of the area, or when more than 1 km² of the area lies more than 1 km inside it; this drops slivers caused by the generalised 1:1,000,000 boundaries. Names are the Finnish names of 2026.
conventions.areaKm2: area of SYKE's delineation (attribute area_m2), including sea where the area is coastal
conventions.sykeAreaNo: SYKE attribute kohdenro; euCode is the Floods Directive APSFR code (attribute apsfrcode)

syke-flood-risk-areas.round: 3rd round: designated by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry on 19 December 2024, for the period to 2030
syke-flood-risk-areas.note: Attribute-only WFS request (no geometry), 64 features: 18 with merkittavyys 'Merkittävä tulvariskialue' (used here) and 46 'Muu tulvariskialue' (other flood risk areas, not significant; not included). Dataset revision 2024-11-12, catalogue metadata modified 2026-01-27. For the municipality overlay, the 18 polygons were fetched once more with geometry (same layer, EPSG:3067).

mmm-2024-decision.name: Suomen merkittävät tulvariskialueet on nimetty (press release, 19 December 2024)
mmm-2024-decision.note: 18 significant areas: 14 on river basins, 4 on the coast. Four earlier areas no longer met the criteria: Loviisa coastal area, Riihimäki city centre, Lapua and Kemijärvi town.

vesi-fi-18-proposed.name: Suomeen ehdotettu 18 merkittävää tulvariskialuetta (22 March 2024)
vesi-fi-18-proposed.note: No new significant areas were proposed in the 3rd round; gives the reasons the four areas were dropped.

syke-laihianjoki-plan.name: Laihianjoen vesistöalueen tulvariskien hallintasuunnitelma vuosille 2022–2027 (Raportteja 47/2021)
syke-laihianjoki-plan.note: Names Laihia, Vaasa and Mustasaari as the municipalities carrying out the plan's measures for the Laihia-Tuovila-Runsor area (e.g. measure 7.2); used to confirm Vaasa, which the boundary overlay put at only 3.7 km².

syke-flood-map.name: SYKE flood map service (Tulvakarttapalvelu, now in the vesi.fi map service)

notes: An area covers only part of a municipality, usually a town centre, village or river valley: the app must say 'part of <municipality> is in a significant flood risk area', never that a given address or building is at risk. SYKE itself says a building inside the delineation is not necessarily at flood risk; only the flood maps show that (syke-flood-map).

Not being in a significant flood risk area does not mean there is no flood risk: the ELY Centres list 46 further 'other flood risk areas' (muu tulvariskialue) in the same dataset, and floods also happen outside both.
No significant stormwater (hulevesitulva) risk areas have been designated: SYKE's catalogue says the municipalities have not named any. Åland has not designated any areas.

3rd round (2024): 18 areas, 14 on river basins and 4 coastal (mmm-2024-decision). No new areas were added; all 18 were already significant in the 2nd round (2018, 22 areas). Dropped in 2024, now 'other flood risk areas' or not listed: Loviisa coastal area, Riihimäki city centre (Riihimäen keskusta), Lapua and Kemijärvi town (Kemijärven kaupunki) (syke-flood-risk-areas, vesi-fi-18-proposed).
Pori is counted by the ministry among the 14 river-basin areas, but SYKE lists both river and sea flooding there (floodTypes river and sea).

Municipality slivers left out after the overlay (under 0.5 km², or lying wholly within 1 km of a generalised boundary): Huittinen area into Kokemäki (3.1 km², none more than 1 km inside; Kokemäki has its own 'other flood risk area'), Ilmajoki-Seinäjoki into Lapua (5.2 km², none more than 1 km inside), Turku coast into Raisio, Kemi coast into Keminmaa and Simo, Helsinki-Espoo coast into Kirkkonummi, Sipoo and Vantaa. These are most likely artefacts of the 1:1,000,000 boundaries but have not been checked against 1:10,000 boundaries.
Kymijoen alaosa reaches into Loviisa (about 52 km²): the Loviisa coastal sea-flood area was dropped in 2024, but the lower Kymijoki river area still covers part of Loviisa.

Ivalon taajama is the village of Ivalo in Inari; Lapväärtti (Lappfjärd) is in Kristiinankaupunki; Ylistaro is part of Seinäjoki and Vähäkyrö part of Vaasa, so Ylistaro-Koivulahti spans Mustasaari, Isokyrö, Vaasa and Seinäjoki.
The ELY Centres became Elinvoimakeskukset in 2025; the sources still call them ELY Centres.
